correctness.rationale: Both first-hit trajectories are solved exactly; fixed section coordinate and return derivative follow algebraically. At μ=4sqrt(2) the normalized map has multiplier −1 and cubic flip coefficient B=9sqrt2−12>0. The local return map is analytic because both crossing speeds are nonzero. Factorization of the second return and nondegenerate cubic reduction yields the local attracting two-cycle and square-root amplitude; reciprocal-square differences give the critical n(x_n−p)^2 limit. Symbolic derivative checker and separate finite numerical tests pass; those tests are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is an exact nontrivial bifurcation threshold for a natural minimal affine replacement of the constant recovery mode in a recently studied two-threshold planar control system. It distinguishes exponential attraction, critical alternating algebraic relaxation with an explicit constant, and a stable two-lap regime in one analytically computable model. The values are not arbitrary low-cost parameter tabulation: the threshold is forced by the stability question and the cubic coefficient quantifies the emergent oscillation.
